description: Anonymous synthetic tasks. Ranking explicitly refers to weighted combined score. Historical v1 fixtures remain unchanged.
transport_request: Produce an English MCM-style synthetic modeling deliverable. Continuous elevator quantity e is in tonnes and bounded by the supplied capacity. Integer n>=0 rocket launches each carry up to the stated kg capacity; unused capacity is permitted. Demand must be met. Elevator cost is c per tonne, launch cost is a fixed F per launch, all costs synthetic currency units. Give a unit-consistent model, ALL nominal optima, both endpoint scenario optima, all optimal-plan switching values in the range and ALL plans tied there. Provide standard-library Python source solve_transport(demand_tonnes, elevator_capacity_tonnes, rocket_capacity_kg, rocket_cost, cost_per_tonne), returning a list of {e_tonnes, launches, cost}; use input arguments. Costs in this test are strictly positive. If you choose exact rational arithmetic, explain how the exact switching price is represented in solver_notes; if using floats, explain tie tolerance. Write Summary 70-110 words and a letter to the logistics manager 130-190 words, consistent with results. Word count uses whitespace-separated tokens containing letters or digits. Stochastic failures are optional inspiration; no probabilities were supplied. Return required_tasks, optional_tasks, nominal_plans, endpoint_plans [{cost_per_tonne, plans}], switches [{cost_per_tonne, plans}], uncertainty_kind, solver_source, solver_notes, latex_model, summary, letter. LaTeX is a directly insertable body fragment in an article with amsmath/amssymb; include math environments and break long equations into short aligned rows. Do not provide a full document or packages. The test page is A4, 12pt, margins 2.5cm; this is a fixture, not a universal contest rule. Do not read files/environment, use network or execute shells. Do not claim code was run or LaTeX compiled.
inference_request: Two contestants have j_B=1-j_A, p_B=1-p_A, and combined scores s_A=alpha*j_A+(1-alpha)*p_A, s_B=alpha*j_B+(1-alpha)*p_B. Official ranking ALWAYS compares combined scores s_A>s_B, not fan shares. In week 1 infer p_A from exact supplied s_A. In an independent rank-only week, the same j_A and alpha are given and A strictly outranks B in COMBINED SCORE; derive the whole fan-share feasibility set within [0,1]. For EACH extra rank_case separately derive the corresponding feasibility set; if no p_A can satisfy the rank, return null interval and explain the inconsistency in results_paragraph. If all p_A are feasible, include both endpoints. Empty feasibility is not a confidence interval and must not be repaired by clipping an invalid threshold to 1. No total votes, sampling distribution or repeated observations were supplied. Spreadsheet zero after elimination is a status placeholder; NA means a future week not held. Explain what those values do and do not imply about support. Return point_share_a, rank_interval_a ({lower, upper, lower_inclusive, upper_inclusive} or null), rank_case_intervals [{case_id, interval}], absolute_votes_identifiable boolean, confidence_interval_available boolean, data_semantics {eliminated_zero, future_na}, results_paragraph, latex_model. Provide directly insertable LaTeX body fragments using math environments and short rows, with separate week variables. Optional bootstrap investigation is not required and cannot invent sampling information.
response_request: Return exactly one valid JSON object with transport and inference objects. Correctly escape LaTeX/code backslashes, quotes and newlines. All task inputs are below; do not call tools. Do not include reference answers, tool checklists or developer process claims in Summary, letter or scientific paragraphs. Use the supplied skill guidance, distinguishing what has been calculated from what has not been run or compiled.
